title: Model Catalog Demo - ZenHealth
summary: Redwood demo of the Model Catalog focused on selecting open models, benchmark comparison, and compatibility matrices. Discussed hosted vs dedicated/private, quantization and latency/cost tradeoffs, and security controls. Agreed next steps for pilot, security docs, and performance benchmarks.
action_items: Alex Rivera - Send tailored pricing and pilot agreement - due 2026-04-20
Priya Shah - Share benchmark spreadsheet and compatibility matrix CSV - due 2026-04-18
Sophie Wu (ZenHealth) - Provide SOC2 and encryption requirements doc - due 2026-04-22
Raj Patel - Provide sample prompt set and traffic pattern stats - due 2026-04-19
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing & pilot docs
Redwood to run a baseline perf test with ZenHealth sample prompts (1k tokens) and share results
Schedule deep-dive on private deployment with ZenHealth infra team w/ calendar invite
ZenHealth to confirm decision timeline (targeting end of May)
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex, Priya, Jordan (Redwood) / John, Maya, Carlos, Sophie, Raj (ZenHealth)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, is this a good time?
[00:04] John: yep, we can start, thanks Alex.
[00:06] Priya: cool, i'll kick off with a very quick agenda; walkthrough the model catalog UI, show how you pick open models, cover benchmarks, compatibility matrices and then a quick look at the API and Redwood Optimize suggestions. leave time for q&a. sound good?
[00:18] Maya: sounds good, we'd like to see how this maps to our latency constraints for telehealth summaries and cost for high-volume inference.
[00:25] Alex: perfect, and lmk if we need to spend more time on security — Sophie, feel free to jump in anytime.
[00:29] Sophie: will do.
[00:31] Priya: alright, screen share coming up — (screen noise) okay so this is the model catalog, top level you can filter by task (chat, completion, embeddings), license (open, commercial), and performance profile. here on the open models tab we surface redwood-verified throughput numbers, quantization compatibility, and a small compatibility matrix showing which hardware families each vectorized kernel supports.
[00:55] Carlos: eh quick Q — how up-to-date are those throughput numbers? like are they representative of our input sizes?
[01:02] Priya: great question, the catalog shows a curated default benchmark (usually 512 tokens, batch size 1 and a medium-length prompt) but you can open the benchmark detail to see perf across sequence lengths and batching. we also have the downloadable spreadsheet — we'll share it after.
[01:18] Maya: when you say quantization compatibility, does that mean the model will run on int8 or 4-bit and have a validated quality delta?
[01:25] Priya: yes, the matrix shows supported quantization modes (int8, 4-bit, q4_0, q4_1 etc) and a quality score delta based on our evals. we flag models where quality drops more than X percent for standard nli/qa evals. there's also a note if the runtime uses special kernels that only work on certain GPUs.
[01:41] John: OK so for us latency is critical — our summarization flow is 95th percentile under 250ms target for short summaries. how do i interpret these numbers in the catalog?
[01:49] Priya: so the catalog shows median per-token latency and throughput on our reference hardware; but we expose a compatibility matrix that maps to HW families (A100, H100, RTX, etc). more importantly you can run the hosted API with your prompt set via our perf sandbox — we can run a baseline and return a latency/cost profile.
[02:06] Alex: to add, we also have routing policies so if you want low latency for a subset of traffic you can route to a high-perf model variant and route other traffic to cheaper quantized variants. that shows up in the Optimize section as suggested batching and cache rules.
[02:19] Raj: about caching — you mean KV cache or prefix cache? we do a lot of doc-level caching upstream.
[02:24] Priya: we mean both; KV cache for autoregressive models and prefix caching for repeated context. the console surfaces estimated cache hit rates and cost savings per route. sometimes in transcripts our docs say "KV cash" haha, that's a known transcription quirk.
[02:37] Maya: sweet, can you show an example of picking a model for embeddings vs picking a model for chat?
[02:41] Priya: sure — switching to embeddings tab — here we recommend models that were tuned for vector similarity (we surface recall/precision numbers vs a few open baselines). for chat/completion there's an additional layer showing hallucination risk score and eval sets used.
[02:53] Jordan: i'll call out the compatibility matrix — if you expand the model details you can download a CSV that maps model -> quantization modes -> supported CUDA kernels -> recommended batch sizes. that's what we usually send to infra teams.
[03:05] Carlos: nice, if we were to bring this on-prem (private deployment) would those quantized kernels still be usable?
[03:11] Priya: depends on the hardware and whether you're using Redwood Private with our private control plane. for example some fuser kernels we ship are optimized for H100 and require driver versions X.Y; the matrix has notes about driver/runtime versions. if you're air-gapped we can provide an on-prem package but there are a few supported combinations only.
[03:29] Sophie: security questions — where are logs stored, and can we forward audit logs to our SIEM?
[03:34] Alex: yes, audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted includes retention policies but we can integrate with your SIEM via secure forwarder and we support KMS-backed encryption and HSM integrations for keys.
[03:44] Sophie: SOC2, SAML SSO?
[03:46] Alex: SOC2 Type II in progress (or recently completed depending on account); we do SAML/SSO and RBAC. we'll attach the security pack.
[03:52] Maya: back to benchmarks — can you show the spreadsheet numbers for a 1k token prompt? that's close to our average.
[03:57] Priya: yep pulling up the benchmark detail — so here's model A (open-llama-34b-ish) at 1k tokens on an A100: median latency 420ms, cost X per 1k tokens, with quantized int8 roughly 30% cheaper but quality delta 1.8% on our eval. model B (redwood-tuned open variant) shows 300ms and lower hallucination on the qa set.
[04:21] John: are those numbers measured with batching enabled? our traffic is bursty, we can't rely on batch aggregation.
[04:26] Priya: these are single-stream median numbers, we also show batched throughput numbers. for bursty traffic you can use our Dedicated pools with autoscaling and burst capacity. the Optimize tab will suggest batching thresholds and when to prefer cache-first paths.
[04:40] Carlos: what's the recommended approach when cost vs latency is the tradeoff?
[04:43] Alex: usually a hybrid: route high-value low-latency traffic to cheaper high-perf hardware or smaller seq-length tuned models, and lower priority traffic to quantized models or cached responses. Redwood's routing policies can do that automatically based on headers/metadata.
[04:56] Maya: any known model that particularly fails the hallucination eval when quantized?
[05:00] Priya: a few Llama variants show bigger deltas at q4_0 compared to q4_1; we flag them. again the catalog has a 'quality delta' column.
[05:08] (brief cross talk)
[05:12] Jordan: quick demo of API usage — (types) here is code snippet: POST /v1/generate model:<model-id> inputs... streaming response example, and you can pass route metadata e.g. x-traffic-tier to select routing policy.
[05:25] Raj: will the client libs handle re-tries and fallback to cheaper models on errors?
[05:29] Alex: yes client SDKs include retry logic and we support automatic fallback policies in the control plane.
[05:34] Sophie: do you log PII in transcripts? our compliance team is worried about data residency.
[05:38] Alex: for Hosted we have configurable retention and redaction options; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and can disable transcript retention entirely. we'll add the exact policy sheet.
[05:49] Maya: curious about the internal evaluations: how big are the eval sets? and can we attach our own evals?
[05:54] Priya: eval sets vary by task; for common tasks we use 2-5k examples. you can absolutely provide your own evals — the console supports custom eval runs and regression alerts. that's part of Redwood Optimize.
[06:07] John: ok show us the Optimize page briefly.
[06:10] Priya: sure — Optimize aggregates telemetry, suggests batching thresholds, recommends quantization profiles per route, and surfaces unit-cost impact. it also ties to quality monitoring so you can set regression alerts on a chosen prompt set.
[06:22] Carlos: do you have example ROI numbers? like how much cost saving teams see when they enable caching and suggested batching?
[06:26] Alex: conservative numbers we've seen: 20-40% cost reduction with prefix/KV caching plus intelligent batching for stateful chat use cases. exact depends on hit rates and prompt distribution.
[06:36] Maya: what's the onboarding path for a pilot? we want to test with 100k tokens/day for 2 weeks.
[06:40] Alex: typical pilot: we provision a small Dedicated pool or Hosted sandbox, run a baseline perf test with your prompts, configure a route in the console, run a 2-week pilot with telemetry, then review regression metrics and cost. we'll supply an SOW/pilot agreement.
[06:54] John: timeline — we need to close infra vendor by end of May, security sign-off mid-May. can you support that?
[06:58] Alex: yes we'll prioritize the security pack and benchmark results.
[07:02] (sounds of note taking)
[07:05] Sophie: please include details on key rotation and HSM options.
[07:07] Alex: will do, noted.
[07:09] Priya: last demo note — when you click into a given model we show per-hardware perf bars, quantization compatibility, eval deltas, and a side-by-side "compatibility matrix" tab. you can export that CSV, and there's a link to the API example and the console route config.
[07:25] Jordan: also including a compatibility matrix for driver/runtime versions and kernel fallbacks — useful for on-prem.
[07:31] Maya: fantastic. any red flags on our side? we run some services in GCP with T4s and some in a private colo with A100s.
[07:39] Priya: T4s will limit some optimized kernels, you'll get lower throughput but quantized models still run. A100/A100s/H100 are best for high throughput/low latency. we'll capture the exact recommended model variants in the CSV.
[07:53] John: are there any constraints on model licensing for open models? we can't ship models that have certain commercial restrictions.
[07:59] Alex: catalog flags license type and we have lawyer-facing docs if you need deeper review. we'll send that.
[08:05] Maya: ok final Q — are there pre-built dashboards for token-level cost breakouts?
[08:09] Priya: yes Console has token-level cost, route-level dashboards, and per-model latency histograms. you can export to CSV or connect to your BI.
[08:19] Alex: great, let's recap next steps. we'll: 1) send pricing & pilot SOW 2) run baseline perf with ZenHealth prompt set 3) share benchmark spreadsheet and compatibility CSV 4) deliver security pack (SOC2/SSO/KMS details) and 5) schedule a private-deploy deep dive with your infra team.
[08:39] John: sounds good, thanks all.
[08:41] Maya: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:43] Alex: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-attributions (Speaker 2/3), auto transcription swapped some product names (eg "Redwood Opti"), timestamps approximate.
